findings.title: XenServer Security Update for CVE-2026-79610, CVE-2026-102700 and CVE-2026-102701
findings.summary_md: Citrix published security advisory CTX697170 on October 13, 2026 for XenServer 8.4 and XenServer 9, rating the bulletin High severity. Three issues may allow a malicious privileged user in a guest VM to compromise or crash the host: CVE-2026-79610, CVE-2026-102700 and CVE-2026-102701, with CVE-2026-102700 affecting XenServer 8.4 only. A fourth issue, CVE-2026-79611, may let an unprivileged guest VM user crash that guest. Updates were pushed to the Early Access and Normal update channels.

findings.title: Xen Security Advisory 517 v2 (CVE-2026-79610) - grant-table: double version change race
findings.summary_md: The Xen.org security team disclosed Xen Security Advisory 517 v2 on October 13, 2026 at 12:28:47 UTC, tracking CVE-2026-79610 as a grant-table double version change race. This upstream researcher disclosure predates the story's first_seen and describes the same guest VM to host compromise vector addressed by the Citrix bulletin.

findings.title: XenServer Security Update for CVE-2026-23554
findings.summary_md: Citrix published advisory CTX696350 on March 17, 2026, an earlier High-severity bulletin for CVE-2026-23554 affecting XenServer 8.4. It warns that privileged code in a guest VM may compromise the host and notes XenServer 9.0 was then in Public Preview and not covered by security bulletins. This prior advisory shows the guest-to-host escape class was documented before the October 2026 round.
